meta.scope: Chile batch 6 — Education statistics (MINEDUC / SIMCE / enrolment), health system (FONASA / ENS / public expenditure), and deeper fiscal detail (DIPRES functional spending, health & education budgets). Completes social and fiscal layers.

candidates.title: Estadísticas de matrícula del sistema escolar (MINEDUC)
candidates.publisher: Ministerio de Educación — Centro de Estudios
candidates.description: Official enrolment statistics of the Chilean school system by level, dependency (municipal, SLEP, subsidised private, private), nationality and special-needs status. Annual series.
candidates.notes: Core education stock statistic. 2025 school enrolment ~3.54 million. Dependency structure and rising foreign-national share are regularly published. Complements CASEN and census education indicators.

candidates.title: Sistema de Medición de la Calidad de la Educación (SIMCE)
candidates.publisher: Agencia de Calidad de la Educación
candidates.description: National standardised assessment of learning outcomes in language, mathematics and other subjects at key grades (4° and 8° básico, II medio). Annual or near-annual public results.
candidates.notes: Flagship learning-outcome indicator. 2025 results show stabilisation/recovery after the post-pandemic drop. Gender gaps and socio-economic gradients are routinely analysed. Continuously cited in education-policy evaluation.

candidates.title: Años de escolaridad promedio / educational attainment indicators
candidates.publisher: INE / Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia / MINEDUC
candidates.description: Average years of schooling of the adult population and related attainment rates, drawn from census, CASEN and administrative sources.
candidates.notes: 2024 marked the first time average schooling of the population 18+ exceeded 12 years (the length of compulsory education). Long upward trend documented in CASEN and census series.

candidates.title: Fondo Nacional de Salud (FONASA) — coverage and expenditure statistics
candidates.description: Public health-insurance fund covering the large majority of the population. Publishes beneficiary counts, benefit expenditure, and modality-of-care statistics (institutional vs free-choice).
candidates.notes: Dominant public insurer (~80% of the population in recent survey frames). Benefit expenditure and per-capita spending are key fiscal and health-system indicators. Copago-cero and GES/AUGE programmes are major policy overlays.

candidates.title: Encuesta Nacional de Salud (ENS) / National Health Survey
candidates.description: Periodic population health survey measuring risk factors, chronic conditions, health-service use and related outcomes. Principal epidemiological input for health policy.
candidates.notes: Structural health-status survey. Complements administrative FONASA and hospital statistics with population-based prevalence and risk-factor data.

candidates.title: Gasto público en salud (DIPRES functional classification)
candidates.description: Public expenditure on health as a share of GDP and in real terms, published in the functional classification of government spending. Includes FONASA, hospital networks and related programmes.
candidates.notes: Health spending rose from 2.6% of GDP in 2005 to 5.3% in 2024 — the largest functional increase over the period. Central fiscal counterpart to the FONASA and provider statistics.

candidates.title: Gasto público en educación (DIPRES functional classification)
candidates.description: Public expenditure on education as a share of GDP and in real terms. Covers school system, higher education and related programmes.
candidates.notes: Education spending rose from 3.2% of GDP in 2005 to 4.9% in 2024. Complements the enrolment and SIMCE statistics with the resource side of the education system.

candidates.title: Clasificación funcional del gasto público (DIPRES)
candidates.description: Official functional breakdown of central-government expenditure (health, education, social protection, etc.) as shares of GDP and in real terms. Used for long-term fiscal sustainability analysis.
candidates.notes: Key analytical product for the composition of the state. Health and education have been the fastest-growing major functions over the last two decades; social protection remains the largest single block.

candidates.title: Isapres — private health-insurance system statistics
candidates.description: Regulatory and statistical reporting on the private health-insurance funds (Isapres): affiliation, premiums, benefits and financial indicators.
candidates.notes: Complement to FONASA. Covers the minority but higher-income segment of the dual health-insurance system. Continuously cited in debates on system fragmentation and reform.

candidates.title: Ley de Presupuestos / National Budget execution statistics
candidates.description: Annual budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues (including copper and lithium) and expenditure by ministry and programme.
candidates.notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links the copper/lithium revenue lines already captured with the functional spending on health, education and social protection.

proposed_edges.basis: SIMCE assesses learning outcomes of the enrolled school population measured by MINEDUC enrolment statistics.
Average years of schooling and attainment rates are regularly derived from CASEN (and census) microdata.
Health is one of the major functions in the DIPRES functional classification of expenditure.
Education is one of the major functions in the DIPRES functional classification of expenditure.
FONASA benefit expenditure is a primary component of public health spending.
The budget law and execution reports are the operational expression of the broader public-finance statistics.
Isapres and FONASA together constitute the dual health-insurance system.
